subject: Sentinel follow-up: region binding scope & ops clarifications
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@sentinelmed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & clarifications: region-binding expectations and ops questions

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a scoped proposal and runbook for your security and infra teams.

Summary from our side:
- Primary ask: ensure patient-identifiable requests from EU datacenters remain within EU (data residency for inference + logs).
- Cross-region failover: you want automatic failover to US only for a predefined subset of low-sensitivity traffic; critical PII requests must not failover without explicit approval.
- Retention: short-term inference logs (for debugging) should be held for 7 days in-region; longer-term audit traces may be archived to encrypted S3 for 365 days.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm?):
1) When you say "patient-identifiable", do you mean any request containing PHI as defined by Sentinel's policy, or only fields matching the redaction list you mentioned?
2) For failover behavior: is a warm-standby EU-only pool acceptable, or do you need automatic cross-region fallback for availability?
3) Legal ops: will Sentinel accept a contractual commitment that PII-resident traffic is pinned to region with documented audit logs (we can provide perms + CIDR ranges)?

Attachments: I attached a first-pass residency_matrix_v1.xlsx to map routes -> pinning options. Monica, Ben — flag anything I missed.

Next steps: Sarah to confirm Q1–Q3; Redwood to produce a short Ops runbook and an options matrix for EU-only vs EU-primary with US fallback.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: residency_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@sentinelmed.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@sentinelmed.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & clarifications: region-binding expectations and ops questions

Logan — thanks for the clear notes and for the matrix. Short answers below, with some follow-ups from Legal Ops.

1) "Patient-identifiable" = any request including patient name, MRN, SSN, scanned notes containing PHI per our internal policy. We also have an allowlist of noise fields where PII is stripped — I'll attach the redaction list separately if helpful.

2) Failover: we need EU-first. Failover to US is allowed only for non-PII traffic and only under an incident declaration from Sentinel SRE. In other words, automatic cross-region fallback for PII is not allowed.

3) Legal Ops would like a contractual commitment for region-pin enforcement and a description of the audit trail we get (fields, retention, access controls)."

Can you also confirm whether Redwood can support key management integration (we use AWS KMS in eu-west-1) and whether logs can be written to a Sentinel-owned bucket in eu-west-1?

I'll loop David (we use him as an external compliance advisor) separately.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Platform Operations | Sentinel Medical
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@sentinelmed.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & clarifications: region-binding expectations and ops questions

Sarah — thanks for the detailed responses. I'm Redwood's solutions engineer for this account; below are technical clarifications and what we can commit to operationally. Long answer but wanted to be explicit so Legal Ops can see the controls.

A. Region pinning model
- We support request-level region pinning by routing policy. For any request flagged as PII (per your redaction list), we can enforce an EU-only route that will only be served by eu-west-1 capacity.
- We implement this with a tenant-tag on the request plus a routing policy: if tenant_tag == "sentinel:pii" -> route to eu-west-1 pool(s).

B. Cross-region failover behavior
- Default: EU pool warm-standby within the same region.
- Controlled failover: For non-PII traffic we can configure automatic cross-region failover to US pools when EU capacity is low. For PII traffic, failover is manual and gated by a Sentinel incident flag (we expose an API you can call to allow emergency routing).

C. Logs, retention, and access control
- Inference request logs (metadata + prompt hashes) can be kept in-region for 7 days for debugging; access controlled via IAM roles.
- Full audit traces (who/when/route) can be exported to a customer-owned S3 bucket in eu-west-1; these exports are encrypted with SSE-KMS. Redwood can integrate with your AWS KMS key for envelope encryption.
- We can redact request bodies before export if you require that.

D. KMS & key management
- Supported: Redwood supports using customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS) in the same region for export encryption. We will surface the key ARN in the private deployment configuration so you retain control.

E. Evidence & contractual language
- We can provide a runbook (Operations play) that documents routing rules, audit fields, and roles with access rights. We cannot change our core SLA to promise zero-possible cross-region replication for backups made for infrastructure durability, but backups of logs exported to your bucket will remain in-region per your retention settings. We'll flag any internal replication for disaster recovery and provide attestations.

Attachments: I attached the SSO/SLA template and a short runbook sketch.

Please let me know if Legal Ops would like a short session to walk through the runbook and KMS steps; happy to schedule a 30-min deep dive.

—Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sso-sla-template.pdf (pdf)]

- We'll produce a scoped proposal (EU-only pinning + manual PII failover runbook) and include an option for EU-primary with constrained US fallback for non-PII.
- I'll include a recommended pricing delta for a dedicated EU pool vs shared capacity (we'll propose both).
- Proposed next step: Legal Ops + Redwood Solutions (Monica) 30-min technical review the week of Nov 9; can Legal Ops suggest 2 windows?

Logan: can you own the proposal doc and share the Drive link when ready? I'll draft the commercial appendix and the deal worksheet.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
